title: A left PCI left V-domain that is not right PCI and not a right V-domain
summary: A countable domain R that is a left PCI ring (every cyclic left module not isomorphic to R is injective) and a left V-ring (every simple left module is injective), but is not right Ore, not a right PCI ring and not a right V-ring. Consequently the opposite ring of R is a right PCI ring that is not left PCI. This answers in the negative the question of Faith (1973), Cozzens and Faith (Simple Noetherian Rings, 1975) and Damiano (1979) whether every right PCI ring is left PCI, and the question, going back to Cozzens and Faith (1975), whether a left V-domain must be a right V-domain. review.reason: Constructs a ring answering open questions about PCI and V-rings.
